Consensus sits at the bottom of the company's range, so a print of about $13M lands inside what management told the market to expect. positioning_check: Short interest is about 8.2M shares with 3.5 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement (curvedtrading via search snippet; the page returned 403 on fetch), and 9.4M / 18.9% of float with 2.9 days to cover around 2026-08-20 (equibles.com/stocks/UMAC). findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 UMAC announced a $16.9M purchase order from Powerus (motors, batteries, cameras, VTX), with no delivery schedule disclosed. That is about 68% of the $25M Q4 internal target set on the 2026-08-06 call. The Upgrade Energy battery acquisition closed 2026-10-19 (earnout pays if Upgrade revenue exceeds $10M), adding a further Q4 revenue source. Both make a reaffirmed Q4 target more likely. The counterweight: UMAC put $30M into Powerus in June 2026 (carried as $30M of cost-method pre-funded warrants in the Q2 10-Q), so the order is partly UMAC's own money coming back.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (2026-08-06, bmo) revenue of $16.7M was 80% above the $9.2M consensus and was paired with a soft Q3 target; the stock fell 5.83%. The $5M Powerus order in April 2026 moved the stock +4% intraday (pulse.bot). On 10-22, the day the $16.9M order was announced, the stock closed -4.18% (stockanalysis history).
findings.why_not_priced: The order is public and the stock fell 36% after it, so the market either discounts it (related-party circularity, no delivery dates) or the sector drawdown swamped it. If the market fully believed in $25M for Q4, a name at about 5.6x annualised Q4 revenue on a ~$560M cap would not have halved in 20 sessions. Confirmation in the release that most of the PO ships in Q4 is the part not yet in the price.
findings.independence: Q4 $25M target from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15395663464719360); Upgrade Energy close and earnout from the 10-23 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1956955/000168316826008046/umac_8k.htm). The $30M Powerus investment comes from the same press release and the Q2 10-Q.

findings.finding: Drone Dominance Gauntlet II named nine drone makers (Neros, Vector, Skycutter, Swarm Defense, XTEND, Perennial, Hyperscale, ModalAI, ORQA US) between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-03. Most order values were still 'pending contract negotiations'. Red Cat's Teal Drones, a disclosed UMAC related-party customer, and Powerus were not among the winners. Management had said its Q4 $25M target rests on Drone Dominance orders 'mostly in Q4' (60,000+ drones in 2H26), so order timing at the OEM level is a risk to the Q4 target and to the 2027 aspiration. XTEND, where UMAC has invested $27.5M, is a winner, which partly offsets this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on Drone Dominance timing. The Q2 print (-5.83%) carried a soft Q3 target explained by capacity build, and the stock sold off.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell from $22 to $17 across the winner announcements. Not priced: which winners UMAC actually supplies, and whether winner contracts were signed in time for Q4 component pulls. The company will state that on the call. If the market had priced a Q4 cut, sell-side targets would already have come down hard. Piper cut only 38 to 29 and Northland initiated outperform at $30 on 10-23.
findings.independence: Tectonic Defense 2026-09-23 (https://www.tectonicdefense.com/scoop-drone-dominance-program-gauntlet-2-winners-secure-big-orders/) says values are pending negotiation. Teal as related party is in the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1956955/000168316826006016/umac_i10q-063026.htm). This is a proxy: UMAC's own supplier relationships with the winners are unconfirmed.

findings.finding: Powerus (PUSA) stock went from $3.88 on 2026-09-30 to about $1.36 intraday on 2026-11-05 (-65%). UMAC carried $30M of cost-method pre-funded warrants ($47.5M measurement-alternative investments in total) plus $39.3M of fair-value equity holdings at 2026-06-30. The release or 10-Q may disclose an impairment or subsequent-event mark on the Powerus position, which would be a non-operating loss of up to about $20M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 other income included a $3.9M unrealized loss and the stock fell 5.8% on that print, but that move cannot be attributed to the line.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates UMAC's investee marks. If the market had priced it, preview EPS estimates would show a wide loss for Q4 rather than about -$0.14. It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Investment carrying values are from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1956955/000168316826006016/umac_i10q-063026.htm). This finding reads the same Powerus relationship as finding 1, but on a different line (balance sheet against revenue). The two do not contradict each other: the order supports revenue, and the investee's equity is impaired.

findings.finding: The 37% 5-day / 49% 20-day drawdown has a documented sector cause rather than a company one. Oct 30: UMAC -12%, RCAT -10%, ONDS -9%, AVAV -6% on a QQQ -4% risk-off. Nov 4: election defense sell-off, with Democrats taking both chambers (KTOS -12.3%, RCAT -10.4%, AVAV -8.3%, UMAC -9%). Nov 5 intraday: UMAC -16.9% with RCAT -15.5%. No company 8-K or adverse filing appeared in the period; the only new filing is a benign Form D for acquisition shares. Combined with about 16% of shares short, any reassurance on Q4 meets a short base positioned for sector beta.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came off a drawdown of this size. The last four reactions were between -5.8% and +5.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sector beta has been treated as company risk. A company-specific leak would show as UMAC falling while peers held, but RCAT fell as much on the same days. The sector selling is itself unfinished (still falling today), so the beta can continue through the window.
findings.independence: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-30 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/30/unusual-machines-sinks-12-red-cat-tumbles-10-as-high-beta-drone-stocks-slide-ondas-drops-9-aerovironment-falls-6/); RCAT tape (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/rcat/history/); EDGAR filing list (Form D 11-02 shows no cash offering).

findings.finding: Management said on 2026-08-06 that Q3 production margins would decline from 34.7% because of introduction costs and the electronics-vendor switch, with low-30s as the near-term goal and a Q4 rebound. A Q3 gross margin in the low 30s is inside what the company told the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 margin of 34.7% (down from 37.4% a year earlier) came with a -5.83% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced, because the company guided it. Filed so the panel sees that a margin dip is the expected outcome, not a miss.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15395663464719360) says 'low 30% gross margin' near term.

findings.finding: At 2026-06-30 UMAC held $229.6M of cash plus $86.8M of investments, $316M in total. Against about 52M shares at $10.83 (~$563M market cap), cash and investments are about 56% of the market value, before Q3 burn (H1 operating cash use was $38.9M) and before any Powerus mark.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a valuation floor, not an edge. It is public, and 'cheap' alone does not move a print. Filed small because the release will restate cash at 9-30.
findings.independence: Q2 shareholder letter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001956955/000168316826006015/umac_ex9901.htm) gives the same cash figure; both rest on one set of financials.

findings.finding: Insiders (CRO, CFO and one other) sold about 48.5k shares (~$1.26M) at about $26 on 2026-08-20 under 10b5-1 plans. There have been no insider purchases into the 49% drawdown: the last Form 4 was 2026-10-06, and the EDGAR list shows no buy cluster.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August insider filings coincided with a -36% slide from mid-August (tikr).
findings.why_not_priced: Old and public. The absence of insider buying at $11 is the only new element, and it is weak.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001956955&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) shows the Form 4/144 dates.

outside_window.finding: The 1,792,012 shares issued to the Upgrade Energy seller at $13.95 (above today's $10.83) carry registration rights: a resale registration must be filed within 30 days of the 10-19 close (~2026-11-18), with effectiveness 60 days after filing if reviewed. That creates a supply overhang of about 3.4% of shares once registered.
A Q4 mark-to-market or conversion of the $30M Powerus pre-funded warrants after PUSA's 65% fall since listing would land in Q4 results (reported ~March 2027) if it is not disclosed now.

Not contradicted as such. It is three months old, the Q2 10-Q was already filed, and there is no evidence it bears on the Q3 release. Listed so the panel can weigh it; it could matter if the new auditor delays the 10-Q.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree with. The 49% run-down is sector beta that peers share, so the company-level evidence (a Q4 PO in hand, but DDP order timing uncertain) neither confirms nor cuts against the tape, and the crowded short tilts any surprise slightly toward squeeze.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range): Powerus PO supports a Q4 target the company already set and is public, cut +1.0 to +0.5.
Rules 5 and 7 (proxy; crowded short against a negative): Gauntlet II order timing is macro-to-company and unconfirmed by UMAC, with about 16% of float short, cut -1.5 to -1.0.
Rule 2 (one-off below operating income): Powerus investee mark cut -0.5 to -0.3.

Rule 5 (positioning and drawdown are not a company fact): sector-drawdown and short-squeeze finding cut +1.0 to +0.5; the cash floor ('cheap is not a finding') cut +0.5 to +0.2; old insider sales cut -0.2 to -0.1.
Core table: p_up moved from 53 to 51 because the lean rests on proxies and partly priced facts. abs_move_pct left at 12 (guidance-update print, thin anchor, Rule 8 against understatement).
